hard: One case in a room at a time.
Turnover after a case is the German cleaning mean for that case's specialty.
A case stays in a room of its own specialty.
A surgeon is in one room at a time, and only in a room they cover.
A case that has not started stays inside that surgeon's hours, 08:00 to 19:00.
A case that has not started is not placed in a closed room or before the current time.
A case that has started keeps its room and its start. It is not interrupted.
Urgent and Immediate cases stay on today's list.
An emergency cannot start before it arrives, and it waits for a free future slot.
Recovery is one bed for a fixed 40 minutes after the case ends. A case the planner can still move must fit the beds that are free.
soft: Overtime after 16:00, counted per minute and summed across rooms.
Idle minutes inside 08:00 to 16:00 that are neither a case nor the turnover after it.
Waiting of Expedited, Urgent and Immediate cases, measured from ready time. Elective waiting has weight 0.
Deferring an Elective or Expedited case off today. This is a deferral, not a permanent cancellation.
Moving a case off the room it had in the previous plan.
An Urgent case starting after 14:00, and an Immediate case starting more than 60 minutes after arrival.
not_modelled: Anaesthesia staff and nursing staff as separate people. The surgeon roster stands in for staffing.
Ward beds, and a full post-anaesthesia unit. The 40-minute bed is a proxy.
A readiness time other than 08:00 for a booked case, or the arrival minute for an emergency.
Patient preference, or a waiting-list rank beyond the four urgency words.

duration_note: Planned minutes are the sum of five published German phase means. A realized length draws each phase on its own and adds the draws. Adding the phase variances would be justified only if the phases were independent. The source publishes each phase on its own and does not say whether they move together, so that independence is an assumption. The VitalDB check compares a 90th percentile with anaesthesia duration, not with room entry to room exit. No file on disk has both of those timestamps, so there is no direct occupancy benchmark.

definitions.overtime_min: Sum across rooms of how far the realized room finish passes 16:00. A room that finishes at 16:00 adds nothing. A closed room adds overtime only if a case still finishes there after 16:00.
definitions.waiting_min: Sum of realized start minus ready time. A booked case is ready at 08:00. An emergency is ready when it arrives. This includes queueing behind earlier cases, not only the slip from the original plan.
definitions.cancellations: Cases deferred off today. They are not recorded as permanently cancelled.
definitions.idle_min: Minutes from 08:00 to 16:00 that are neither a case nor the turnover gap after it. Empty time in a closed room is included as idle. There is no separate unavailability term.
definitions.pacu_queue_min: Bed-minutes of recovery occupancy above the bed limit. It is not a count of patients. A recovery disruption lowers the limit at the event.
definitions.changes: Cases deferred, moved, added, or shifted by 15 minutes or more.
definitions.violations: Broken hard constraints in the published plan after the disruption has been applied. A packed list can fail this check. A recovery plan is checked again after the replan.
definitions.executed_violations: Broken rules on the realized timeline: overlap, a missing turnover gap, a double-booked surgeon, an incompatible room, or a start before the case was ready. Finishing after 16:00 is overtime, not one of these.
definitions.urgent_waiting_min: Waiting from ready time, Urgent and Immediate cases only.
definitions.deferred_min: Actual surgical minutes of the cases moved off today. Overtime that falls only because this rises is work moved, not time saved.
definitions.finish_error_min: Average gap between each room's published finish and its actual finish.
definitions.late_start_min: Average minutes a case started after the time on the published list.
definitions.weighted_cost: Overtime, idle, deferrals and urgency-weighted waiting under the weights in the table, as one number. It is what the solver is asked to minimise, scored on the day as played.
definitions.recovery: CP-SAT plan, then a new CP-SAT after each disruption. The planner sees estimated ends for cases still running, never their actual end. The comparison is the same morning plan handled by the manual rule: keep the order, give an emergency the next free turn, slide later cases.

extensions.note: These checks use the first 24 development seeds, six of each single disruption. They are the same days as the start of the 100-day run. They show whether the tradeoff moves when the weights, the clock time, or the duration assumption changes. They are not a larger hospital sample.

provenance.definition: Actual anaesthesia minutes of VitalDB patients held out of training. Day composition is simulated.
provenance.turnover: German 2019 OR cleaning mean, not part of the case

duration_model.target: Anaesthesia time in minutes (anaesthesia start to end). Closest VitalDB field to room occupancy; not room entry to exit.
duration_model.source: VitalDB clinical table, Seoul National University Hospital (Lee et al., Scientific Data 2022). Scores only; no VitalDB row is stored here.
duration_model.features: Booked operation, department, approach, position, anaesthesia type, age, sex, size, ASA, emergency flag, hypertension, diabetes, pre-operative labs. Nothing recorded during or after surgery.
duration_model.split: By patient: 60% train, 20% calibration, 20% test. No patient is in two parts.
duration_model.model: Gradient-boosted quantile trees (scikit-learn HistGradientBoosting, P10/P50/P90 on log minutes) with a split-conformal correction for 80% coverage.

ml_planning.note: Each day is a simulated list of real VitalDB patients the model never trained on, played with their actual anaesthesia minutes. Every basis plans the same list with the same solver and weights. VitalDB is one Korean academic hospital; a different hospital needs its own training data.
